hero.title: Master's in Computer Engineering in Canada for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: Pursue an MASc or MEng in Computer Engineering in Canada across top research universities, conducting advanced research in SoC architecture, embedded AI, and quantum computing with up to 3 years of PGWP work authorization.

highlights.eligibility: Recognised academic qualification + IELTS / TOEFL / PTE proficiency

overview: Pursuing a master's degree in Computer Engineering in Canada places graduate students at the forefront of advanced hardware research, quantum computing development, and embedded systems engineering. Canadian research institutions maintain close partnerships with global semiconductor leaders and government research agencies, offering world-class infrastructure for advanced physical and logical computing systems.

Canadian universities deliver research-focused Master of Applied Science (MASc, 2 years) and professional Master of Engineering (MEng, 1 to 1.5 years) programs. Core specializations span VLSI Systems Design, Embedded Machine Learning, High-Performance Computer Architecture, Fault-Tolerant Computing, and Robotics Hardware, with MASc students receiving graduate research assistantships and publishing in premier IEEE and ACM engineering conferences.

Graduates step directly into senior engineering roles such as Hardware Systems Architect, Semiconductor Test Engineer, and FPGA Verification Lead across Canada's growing hardware technology corridors in Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, and Ottawa. Under Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) regulations, graduates of qualifying full-time post-secondary degree programs at designated learning institutions (DLIs) may be eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) for up to three years (the exact duration depends on program length, institution eligibility, and meeting language and study conditions; issuance is non-automatic).

sections.title: Why Study Computer Engineering in Canada ?
sections.lead: Students interested in computer architecture, robotics, embedded systems, software-hardware interaction, computer hardware, and intelligent technologies frequently travel to Canada. In Canada, computer engineering integrates computer science and electrical engineering concepts to create, develop, test and enhance computer systems.

items: Depending on their prior credentials and professional aspirations, students can pursue undergraduate or graduate degrees. Engineering labs, research projects, design courses, and, at some schools, co-ops are among ways that Canadian universities provide learning opportunities.
Key advantages of studying Computer Engineering Education in Canada
Learn about digital systems, embedded computers, microprocessors, and computer architecture through advanced technical education.
Comprehend the relationship between computer hardware, operating systems, software, and networks.
The Internet of Things (IoT), robots, cybersecurity, autonomous systems, and artificial intelligence hardware are examples of emerging technologies.
Engage in engineering projects, system design, simulation, and laboratory work to gain practical knowledge.
Investigate computer vision, intelligent systems, integrated circuits, and high-performance computing.
Industry Exposure: A few programs provide internships or co-ops with engineering and technology companies.
Prepare for professions in computer systems, electronics, embedded systems, hardware development, and related technical industries.

sections.title: Qualifications for Computer Engineering Study in Canada
sections.lead: Whether students apply for a postgraduate program after earning a bachelor's degree or an undergraduate degree after Class 12 determines the eligibility requirements.

items: Academic Requirement - A bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a similar discipline that the program accepts
Academic Performance
Relevant Coursework - Depending on the program, prerequisites may include math, programming, digital systems, electronics, or other subjects.
English Proficiency - TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, IELTS Academic or another recognized exam
IELTS score: Generally between 6.5 and 7.0, depending on the school

pairs.d: Not always necessary, but required by some programs or specific applicants

sections.title: Computer Engineering Admission Requirements in Canada
sections.lead: The requirements for admission differ depending on the university, specialization, and degree level. Before submitting an application, candidates should review the official program criteria.

items: Academic Writings
For candidates seeking postgraduate degrees:
A certificate of bachelor's degree.
Official transcripts and grades from the university.
A degree grading system, upon request.
Proof of pertinent prerequisite coursework.
Verification of interim results or degree completion, if relevant.

Candidates may require the TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, IELTS Academic, or another recognized English language exam. Institutions and programs have different requirements for scores and procedures regarding exemptions.
Depending on the university and degree level, candidates can require:
A valid passport number.
A purpose statement or more application responses.
Letters of recommendation, if necessary.
When required, a curriculum vitae or resume for postgraduate applications.
GRE scores, if relevant.
A statement of research interests or a research proposal for certain research initiatives.
A technical project portfolio, upon request.
Completed the application and paid the application cost.

sections.title: Admission Procedure for Computer Engineering in Canada
sections.lead: These steps can be used by students who intend to study Computer Engineering in Canada.

items.title: Select Your Level of Study
items.desc: After obtaining an appropriate undergraduate degree, choose between pursuing a bachelor's degree and a master's degree.

items.title: Choose Your Area of Expertise
items.desc: Determine your areas of interest, such as communications, embedded systems, computer architecture, electronics, robotics, hardware design, or intelligent computing systems.

items.title: Make a shortlist of universities
items.desc: Examine academic requirements, location, co-ops, research possibilities, accreditation, curriculum, and tuition costs.

items.title: Verify Your Eligibility
items.desc: Examine prerequisite courses, English language proficiency, GRE requirements, academic grade criteria, and application dates.

items.title: Prepare the application materials
items.desc: Organize the necessary documents, such as transcripts, certifications, passport information, English test scores, and references.

items.title: Send in Your Applications
items.desc: Use the appropriate provincial application system or the official university portal to submit an application. Pay the application fee and keep an eye on any developments.

items.title: Accept and Examine Your Offer
items.desc: Verify the requirements for admission, the start date, the tuition deposit, the scholarship information, and the deadlines. As instructed by the institution, accept the offer.

items.title: Make a financial plan
items.desc: Before making any financial commitments, figure out the cost of tuition and living expenses, set up the necessary documentation, and go over the available scholarships.

items.title: Submit an application for a study permit in Canada
items.desc: Observe Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's (IRCC) current regulations. Unless there is an exemption, a provincial or territorial attestation letter might be necessary. Admission to a university does not ensure that a study permit will be granted.

items.title: Get Ready to Arrive
items.desc: Make travel, lodging, health insurance, and university enrollment arrangements.

sections.title: Professional Recognition and Accreditation
sections.lead: For students who want to work as engineers in Canada, accreditation -

items: Key Points
Verify whether the Canadian Engineering Accreditation Board (CEAB) has accredited a particular bachelor's degree in computer engineering or computer systems engineering.
Program Specific Status: Not all engineering degrees offered by universities are automatically accredited.
The completion of a master's degree does not inevitably result in the accreditation of an unaccredited undergraduate engineering degree.
A Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) license is not automatically granted by a degree alone.
Each Canadian province or territory has regulators in charge of overseeing engineering licensing.
A P.Eng. is not necessary for many computer hardware and technology jobs. license, however prerequisites vary according to the position and its duties.

sections.lead: University, program, degree level, and immigration conditions all have different document needs.

items: Academic Writings

Proof of degree completion or interim results.
Extra academic records, if the university requests them.
A current passport.
Test results in English, if necessary.

Financial Records and Study Permit

Forms and supporting documentation for immigration applications.
If necessary, a police certificate or medical checkup.
When appropriate, biometrics.
Before filing an application, candidates should verify the most recent requirements and consult the official IRCC checklist for their situation.

faq.q: After Class 12, are Indian students able to pursue computer engineering studies in Canada?
faq.a: Indeed. After Class 12, Indian students who fulfill the academic requirements of the university which often include mathematics, physics, and occasionally chemistry can apply to undergraduate computer engineering programs.

faq.q: How long do computer engineering courses last in Canada?
faq.a: The majority of undergraduate degrees in computer engineering take four years to complete. Depending on the university and whether the program is course-based or research-based, postgraduate master's programs typically last one to two years.
faq.question: How long do computer engineering courses last in Canada?

faq.q: What distinguishes Canadian computer science from computer engineering?
faq.a: Indeed. Computer hardware, digital systems, embedded technologies, and the combination of hardware and software are the main topics of computer engineering. Although certain topics overlap, computer science places a greater emphasis on algorithms, software, computation, and programming.

faq.q: How much does it cost Indian students to study computer engineering in Canada?
faq.a: Undergraduate tuition may cost between CAD 35,000 and CAD 75,000 or more per year, while postgraduate tuition may cost between CAD 20,000 and CAD 60,000 or more, according to a general planning estimate. Living expenses are extra, and each institution has different actual prices.

faq.q: Question 5. After earning my computer engineering degree, can I get employment in Canada?
faq.a: Depending on their program, school, academic background, and current IRCC standards, some graduates may be eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP). A work permit, job, or permanent residence are not always assured by a Canadian degree.
